=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20995-20998 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The standalone sweep-only branch exits before `prime_phase_concurrency_snapshot` runs, leaving concurrency caps disabled for idle-tick recovery dispatches.
  WHY: With `PHASE_CAPS_ENABLED` false, `phase_cap_can_dispatch` allows dispatches, so standalone recovery can bypass configured `.github/ai/concurrency_caps.yml` limits that are honored on busy ticks.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:296-299 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The OpenCode CLI setup remains gated on an active tracking issue even though idle-tick standalone recovery can invoke an OpenCode stall judge.
  WHY: On an idle tick the skipped setup leaves the models.dev cache unavailable, so the judge can fail isolation and eventually escalate the standalone issue to `ai:needs-human` instead of recovering it.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1090-1092 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `continue-on-error: true` can leave the workflow run successful when standalone recovery exits nonzero.
  WHY: Workflow-status monitoring may not distinguish a failed recovery from a successful tick; Claude Sonnet regarded this as a documented tradeoff rather than a defect.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1090-1100 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When the support checkout lacks the standalone-recovery branch, the grep guard warns and exits successfully while the recovery step does nothing, leaving the activation gap unclosed without an operator-visible drift signal.
  WHY: A consumer pinned to older support can upgrade its wrapper without gaining the recovery behavior until its pinned SHA advances.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20995-20998 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The sweep-only branch exits before the concurrency-cap snapshot is primed, leaving `PHASE_CAPS_ENABLED` at its default `false`.
  WHY: On idle ticks, standalone recovery dispatches without checking `.github/ai/concurrency_caps.yml`, although busy ticks honor the caps.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:296-301 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The OpenCode install step requires `has_work == 'true'`, but idle-tick standalone recovery can reach `run_stall_judge`.
  WHY: The judge can need OpenCode when the issue has `ai:codex`, the role selects codex, or Claude returns exit 75; without setup, configuration fails and repeated failures can escalate the issue to `ai:needs-human`.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `continue-on-error: true` makes failures in the new standalone-recovery step non-fatal.
  WHY: A failed recovery leaves the issue unrecovered while the scheduled run stays green; this is a documented tradeoff, not a defect, because later sweeps still run and recovery errors appear in the step log.

  PROBLEM: `continue-on-error: true` can hide a fatal poller failure at the job-conclusion level.
  WHY: A nonzero poller exit leaves the Actions run successful, so operators relying on workflow failures may not see that recovery failed.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1090-1100 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The support-version grep guard can warn and exit successfully when the standalone-recovery branch is absent, leaving the recovery step a no-op without a drift signal.
  WHY: Consumers pinned to older support may not get the new recovery behavior until their pinned SHA advances.

The agents.d fragment and changelog fragment claim the `--origin-repo` gap was already fixed on main, but the review states that claim was not verified against the current ref.
